name: Learn dice stacking
blurb: Scooping dice into a cup and setting them down as a perfect tower. It looks like sleight of hand and is actually centrifugal force plus a lot of practice.
gear: Four or five large casino-style dice
A dice cup with a straight interior
steps: Learn the scoop: sweep the cup across the table to gather the dice inside in one motion.
Learn the spin: circle the cup so the dice ride the wall and stack themselves against the inside.
Practise with two dice until the stack is reliable, then add one at a time.
Learn the set-down — the moment you stop the spin and place the cup — which is where most stacks collapse.
Practise on a soft surface, which is quieter and keeps the dice from bouncing away.
Work up to four or five dice and then to picking the stack up again.
tips: The cup shape matters enormously. A tapered cup makes this nearly impossible.
Speed of the spin is the main variable. Too slow and they fall, too fast and they climb out.
proof: A clean stack of four dice in one motion, three times in a row.
